candidates.title: Sunset Limited derails after grade-crossing collision in Louisiana (updated)
candidates.excerpt: BROUSSARD, La. — Amtrak’s Sunset Limited derailed today (Sunday, Nov. 22) in Broussard after a grade crossing collision with a truck carrying a bulldozer, KSLA-TV reports. An Amtrak statement said the derailment occurred about 6:15 p.m. and that the train’s locomotives and two baggage cars derailed, but all passenger cars remained upright. There were 95 passengers on board; bus transportation will be provided to their destination. Acadian Ambulance said in a Facebook post that it sent 12 ambulances to the scene and transported four patients to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Seven ambulance crews remained at the scene to triage and treat other passengers. The Lafayette Fire Department said in a later Facebook post that at least five people had suffered minor injuries. candidates.title: News photos: CSX Santa Train gets patriotic
candidates.excerpt: KINGSPORT, Tenn. — The CSX Santa Train, an Appalachian tradition dating to its Clinchfield Railroad debut in 1943, featured the railroad’s two America 250 locomotives on Saturday, Nov. 21, during its annual 110-mile trip through Kentucky, Virginia, and Tennessee on. CM44AH locomotives Nos. 250 and 2025, along with one of the railroad’s executive train F40s, led the journey from Shelby, Ky., to Kingsport. The Kingsport Times News reports that during its 84th trip, the train distributed more than 15,000 toys, 6,000 train safety books, and 5,700 backpacks filled with gifts, gloves, and hats. “With that many years going on, we have families coming back over and over, and then they bring their kids, and then they bring their grandkids,” Angela Costa, CSX senior manager of community investment, told the newspaper. “CSX is just so excited to continue that tradition with the 2026 CSX Santa Train.” — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. candidates.title: Equinor and NCL extend low-carbon marine fuel agreement
candidates.excerpt: Equinor and North Sea Container Line (NCL) have extended their collaboration on low-carbon marine fuels into 2027. Under the extended agreement, Equinor will continue supplying low-carbon bunker fuel from its Tjeldbergodden industrial plant in Norway to NCL’s dual-fuel methanol container vessels, NCL Vestland and NCL Nordland. The companies began working together during 2026, establishing a direct supply chain between the fuel production facility and NCL’s container shipping operations. Biomethanol production at Tjeldbergodden Equinor’s Tjeldbergodden plant is certified to produce biomethanol using mass-balanced biomethane supplied by European Union producers through the interconnected European gas grid. The arrangement allows NCL’s two vessels to continue using lower-carbon fuel while operating along the Norwegian coastline. Equinor and NCL said the extended cooperation will support the commercial use of alternative marine fuels and the development of lower-emission logistics corridor

candidates.title: Samudera and CONCOR sign agency agreement for EXIM cargo
candidates.excerpt: Samudera has signed an agency agreement with Container Corporation of India Ltd (CONCOR) aimed at improving coordination between inland logistics and international shipping services. The agreement was formalised at CONCOR’s head office in New Delhi on 26 October 2026. Under the arrangement, the companies will support export-import cargo movements across markets including India, Thailand, Malaysia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates and Indonesia. The cooperation combines CONCOR’s inland logistics capabilities with Samudera’s established regional shipping network. It is also expected to provide a basis for exploring additional markets and expanding CONCOR’s overseas reach. Samudera and CONCOR said they intend to expand shipping activities and provide customers with more integrated logistics solutions. The announcement does not specify any new liner service, port rotation, implementation schedule or financial terms associated with the agreement.

candidates.excerpt: Cargo disruptions and sensitive data theft have emerged as the leading concerns among shipping industry readers when considering the consequences of cyberattacks, according to the latest Container News Readers Speak poll. Asked what concerns them most about cyberattacks in shipping, respondents placed operational disruption narrowly ahead of data theft. Financial losses and the erosion of customer trust also attracted attention, suggesting that concerns extend beyond the immediate technical consequences of a security breach. Cargo disruptions emerge as the leading concern The strongest support went to cargo disruptions, reflecting the importance of operational continuity in container shipping. The vessels are being sought for a proposed joint venture involving state-owned energy companies Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum. candidates.excerpt: Semaf calls off Renfe drivers’ strike after deal with Spanish ministry The Spanish train drivers’ union Semaf has called off the Renfe strike planned for Monday 23 November, which would also have hit Renfe Mercancías freight trains. The union reached a safety agreement with the Spanish Ministry of Transport on 20 November. Semaf was the last union still maintaining the strike call, as the other Renfe and Adif unions had reportedly already ended their protests. The 23 November stoppage itself replaced an earlier strike day, which Semaf postponed after the government approved extra safety measures. The breakthrough came with a new protocol for adverse weather, based on thresholds from forecasts by the Spanish State Meteorological Agency (Aemet). Semaf also secured new rules for faults in the LZB and ERTMS signalling systems, daily publication of temporary speed restrictions and earlier retirement for rail staff. candidates.title: Record tram orders: how Stadler, Škoda, CAF and Alstom dominate Europe’s renewal wave
candidates.excerpt: Record tram orders: how Stadler, Škoda, CAF and Alstom dominate Europe’s renewal wave In a revival of Railway Gazette International’s survey of tram and light rail vehicle orders, Michael Dreyer analyses the trends that are shaping the next wave of urban rail rolling stock procurement in Europe and beyond. The global tram and light rail vehicle market is entering a second major renewal wave. The first large-scale generation of low-floor vehicles was introduced mainly during the 1990s and early 2000s; many of these fleets are now 20 to 30 years old and approaching life expiry. This is creating substantial renewal demand alongside continued investment in new tram and light rail infrastructure. Europe remains the core market, but demand is increasingly spreading to Latin America, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and North America. Volumes to Alaska increased by 0.6%, while those to Hawaii decreased by 5.4%. In October, full imports grew by 13.1% compared with the same month last year. Total international and domestic volumes reached 235,210 TEU, up 0.5% year-on-year. Breakbulk volumes reached 345,075 tonnes in the first 10 months of the year, up 12.2%, supported by continued strong industrial demand. Auto volumes totalled 224,416 units, down 2.2% compared with the same period in 2025. “Tariff impact on the industry is being offset by an increase in diverted auto units from Canada due to congestion,” NWSA said. US rail traffic rises 7.3% as intermodal gains 10.7% in latest week
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%. candidates.title: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom
candidates.excerpt: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom Private credit is gaining ground in Asia as demand for flexible capital grows and the AI boom needs funding, according to KKR. Asia has historically relied on banks for credit, and they still provide 88 per cent of the region’s debt capital, compared with 50 per cent in Europe and just 31 per cent in the US. However, forces reshaping Japan and driving investment in AI infrastructure are starting to change this, KKR said in a recent blog post. In the US and Europe, regulators have made banks retrench, but that is not happening in Asia. Instead, private credit is in demand across the region because it offers flexible capital alongside banks that remain deeply embedded in corporate financing. KKR argued that Asian banks provide cheap but inflexible capital, and that private credit was plugging this gap. AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending November 14, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) has reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending November 14, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 529,919 carloads and intermodal units, up 7.3 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending November 14 were 230,260 carloads, up 3.3 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 299,659 containers and trailers, up 10.7 percent compared to 2025. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included motor vehicles and parts, up 2,182 carloads, to 15,691; metallic ores and metals, up 1,979 carloads, to 20,470; and petroleum and petroleum products, up 1,063 carloads, to 11,362. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 1,205 carloads, to 24,396; and miscellaneous carloads, down 239 carloads, to 8,801. candidates.title: Domestically produced Russian high speed train to be tested in 2027
candidates.excerpt: Domestically produced Russian high speed train to be tested in 2027 RUSSIA: Ural Locomotives is advancing development of the prototype EVS360 Bely Krechet (White Gyrfalcon) high speed trainset, with Russian Railways expecting it to be delivered for testing during 2027. The Bely Krechet project being undertaken by Sinara Group’s Ural Locomotives subsidiary in partnership with mostly Russian suppliers covers the development and production of 43 eight-car trainsets for the planned Moskva – St Petersburg high speed line. Two prototype trainsets are to be produced ahead of the 41 production units, with deliveries scheduled for 2028-30. The EVS360 is intended for operation at up to 360 km/h, with a maximum design speed of 400 km/h. The eight-car train will accommodate approximately 454 passengers in four classes, with a bistro car also provided. Union Pacific police in shootout after alleged train robbery on southern California freight line
candidates.excerpt: Two men were arrested after a shooting involving Union Pacific Railroad Police investigating suspected cargo theft near the busy Tehachapi Loop on Nov. 12. No injuries were reported, according to the Kern County Sheriff’s Office and reported in local media. The shooting occurred about 10:40 p.m. near Highway 58 and Broome Road, east of the loop. Railroad (NYSE: UNP) police were patrolling the area in response to recent thefts from trains when they discovered an open cargo-container door, authorities said. Officers began investigating, and a shooting occurred, according to the sheriff’s account. A suspect fled on foot, and railroad police secured the area and requested assistance from the sheriff’s office. Kern County detectives responded and took over the investigation. Investigators subsequently located Jesus Rodriguez, 32, in Keene and arrested him. Genesee & Wyoming prepares to split into three rail holding companies
candidates.excerpt: Genesee & Wyoming Inc. is planning to separate into three rail holding companies, effective Jan. 1, 2027, a move that will position the regional entities for eventual sale. The companies will continue to be owned by G&W parent Brookfield and GIC. G&W operates more than 100 railroads. The new companies are: Atlantic & Great Lakes Transportation Inc., which will be made up of G&W operations in New England (including Berkshire & Eastern Railroad), New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. Atlantic & Great Lakes will be based in Rochester, N.Y., and led by Chief Executive Bill Keough, who has been with G&W for eight years and most recently served as regional senior vice president. Canyon & Cascade Transportation Inc., which will be comprised of G&W operations in Washington, Oregon, California, Arizona, and New Mexico.
